doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Cutting contests and legato swing
summary: Roker says cutting was before his time and that only players who could not swing got cut; jazz should be fluid and legato.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Now that’s something else I want to talk with you about because see this is all a part of the education of jazz is the cutting contest.
Well that was more or less before my time. That cutting stuff. When I came along, cats were friendly and they were willing to help you.
Oh it wasn’t always to the death—
I know verbally cutting — cats cut each other up musically. Is that what you’re talking about?

Well that only happened to people who couldn’t swing. They would get cut up. Because they would ruin the groove. That’s what I mean about the blues. If you get a guy and he get on the bandstand and he play [scats] if he plays too staccato, guys would cut him up. Because it should be more liquid, fluid you know? Not so staccato, you know what I’m saying? Jazz is more legato.
I mean and then you instill a few staccato, just for the differences, you know to show your classical training or awareness you know? But it’s more legato instead of staccato.
